svg.title: How #63350 and #63351 make room for a voice turn
svg.desc: Panel a: a caller's speech goes to speech to text, then to vLLM 0.32's scheduler, which carries the two changes, then to text to speech and back to the caller; 24 coding-agent sessions send their requests to the same scheduler at priority 2, the voice turn's at priority 0; the scheduler allocates from the KV pool beneath it. Panel b, #63350, a pool of 12 KV blocks: two agent requests hold 5 each and 2 are free, while a voice turn that needs 4 waits beside the pool; on stock vLLM it waits for an agent request to finish, while #63350 preempts the latest agent request, agent B, and the turn takes 4 of its blocks; agent B waits, its KV kept in the CPU tier for its resume. Panel c, #63351, the engine's steps in time, one box a step, from the reply's first token: without #63351 each step of the reply also carries an agent's prefill chunk, so in the time #63351 gives the reply its first 48 tokens the reply gets 14 without it; after the window, agent prefill resumes. Blocks and steps are illustrative.
svg.text: One GPU: a voice agent beside coding agents
The turn waits for an agent request to finish.
Agent B waits; its KV stays in the CPU tier for its resume.
time, one box per engine step, from the reply's first token
